messages:
alice: Deployed Triton 2.1.1 to cluster-a ~18:02 UTC. Seeing 2-3x tail latency on short-seq requests (seq<=64). Anyone else?

 david: Yup, spike on prod-gpu-pool started ~18:05. SLOs breached for a few routes. Can we rollback?

 alice: Not yet — collecting more traces. Can @frank or @erin pull runtime kernel selection logs and nvprof traces?

 frank: On it. Triton selector picked 'fmha_flash' for our gpt2-ish shapes. Prior default was 'cutlass_fmha'.

 erin: nvprof snippet attached:
```
TRITON_SELECTOR: selected_kernel=fmha_flash sm=80 batch=8 seqlen=32
kernel_time_ms=2.52
prev_kernel=cutlass_fmha kernel_time_ms_prev=0.89
```

 bob: That selector change came from the autotuner PR merged last week (optimize for high throughput). cc @infra-sig

 alice: :thinking_face: Interesting — our traffic is mostly short sequences. Could autotuner be biasing towards long-seq perf and picking wrong kernels for our workload?

 frank: Also saw KV cache stats: hit_rate fell from 98% -> 86% post-change, and batching heuristics emitted more single-request batches.

 david: Quick mitigation: forcing kernel override to 'cutlass_fmha' for seqlen<=64 in runtime config. Deploying now.

 deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime-config-kernel-override id=abc123

 erin: After override p95/tail latencies returned to baseline. Root cause hypothesis: selector scoring favored kernels with better large-seq throughput but worse small-seq latency and memory use, leading to lower cache locality and batching.

 alice: Action items:
1) frank: revert autotuner PR until we patch selector logic
2) erin + bob: add seqlen-aware weight to selector heuristics
3) david: add short-seq latency regression test in CI and add perf check to release gating
I'll open tickets and track.

 frank: Opened RW-5421 with traces and profiler links: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/5421 :eyes:

 alice: Thanks everyone. Monitoring for 30m, will close if stable :thumbsup:
